answer: Require each identity to compute a verifiable delay function keyed to its own address every epoch — an inherently sequential climb up a trellis that no amount of added cores can shorten, though a verifier checks the result in an instant like tasting a drop of nectar. Because the delay cannot be sped up and the keyed puzzle cannot be shared between personas, every fake costs the same irreducible wall-clock span. A single host clears at most (cores × window ÷ delay) identities per epoch — a hard nadir on how many personas one machine can carry before the beacon-timed window closes on the rest.
